prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S026: The Station Supervisory Control System is named Glasswing in this document.
S027: The Station Supervisory Control System presents available station and bay indications through a consolidated operator interface.
S028: Its displays show operating conditions and communication quality without replacing local equipment indications.
S029: The Station Gateway carries supervisory communications between station-level functions and remote operations interfaces.
S030: Supervisory visibility depends on the availability and quality of the underlying communications and status inputs.
S031: The supervisory layer does not perform the protective functions assigned to dedicated protection equipment.
S032: The Control Room Operator uses the supervisory displays to assess station conditions and coordinate operating actions.
S033: Any supervisory command remains subject to configured permissions and the applicable operating procedure.
S034: Local interlocks and equipment-level control logic remain authoritative for permitted switching actions.
S035: A communications interruption can leave displayed information stale or temporarily unavailable.
S036: After communications recover, operators confirm that indications are current before relying on them for decisions.
S037: The Satellite Time Receiver is named Bluefin in this document.
S038: The Satellite Time Receiver acquires a reference from supported satellite timing signals.
S039: It distributes time to station equipment over the configured time-distribution network.
S040: Time distribution supports consistent event timestamps across equipment that receives and applies the reference.
S041: Accurate timestamps assist event correlation but do not establish the validity of an electrical measurement or protection decision.
S042: If the external timing reference is lost, equipment behavior depends on its individual clock and holdover capabilities.
S043: Holdover performance varies by device and may degrade as the interval without a valid reference increases.
S044: The Satellite Time Receiver produces the Clock Drift Snapshot when its measured offset meets the configured reporting condition.
S045: Time-quality indications allow operators to distinguish synchronized operation from degraded or unavailable timing.
S046: The Station DC System supplies operating power to station automation equipment within its designed capacity.
S047: A loss of station power can interrupt supervisory visibility and time distribution until supported supplies are restored.
S048: The Station Supervisory Control System produces the Alarm Acknowledgement Slip for supervisory recordkeeping.
S049: The Substation Supervisor oversees operational use of the supervisory system and escalation of unresolved availability concerns.
S050: The Feeder Protection Relay is known as Tandem in this concept.
S051: The Protection Relay Engineer is known as Larkspur in this concept.
